## Background

I trained as a computer scientist before coming to MDS, studying computer science at
National Tsing Hua University in Taiwan. Most of my degree was spent on the software
side of things — algorithms, systems, and enough coursework in machine learning to
know that I liked it and did not yet understand it properly.

What I took away was a habit more than a subject: build the thing, run it, and let
the result tell you whether you were right. That habit turned out to transfer
directly to data science, where the temptation to trust a number you have not
checked is considerably stronger.

## Why data science

The turning point was noticing how often the hard part of a technical problem was
not the code. A model would train and report a number, and the real question — does
this number mean what we think it means, and would it hold up on next month's data —
was the one nobody had the tools to answer.

That is what MDS is for me: filling in the statistical half of a problem I had only
been solving from the engineering side. Experiment design, inference, and knowing
when a result is genuinely there rather than an artifact of how the data was
collected.

## What I work with

- **Languages** — Python, R, SQL
- **Tooling** — Git and GitHub, the Unix shell, Quarto, Jupyter, conda
- **Areas** — machine learning, statistical inference, data visualization,
  reproducible workflows

This list is going to change over the year. I would rather it reflect what I have
actually used than what I have heard of, so I update it as the program goes.

## Where I am headed

I am aiming for a **machine learning engineer** or **data scientist** role after
MDS. The work I want is the kind where the same person frames the question, builds
the model, and is still around when it goes to production — my background is a
reasonable fit for that, and MDS is filling in the part I was missing.

## Outside of data science

Vancouver has been an adjustment in the best way. Coming from Taiwan, the scale of
the mountains sitting at the end of the street still catches me off guard, and I
have been using weekends to get out into them.
